acceptance: Splitting a pane puts a new pane on the requested side and focuses it, recursively; closing a pane folds its parent split and keeps the surviving focus; a pane dropped on a side of another lands there without its editor appearing twice; reordering siblings keeps their split's identity, and dropping a pane back into its own slot changes nothing.

Moving a folder rebinds every open document under it, deleting one closes exactly its document subtree, and a restored layout keeps its ratios within 0.15..0.85 and restores a pane whose document is gone as an empty pane.

An editor is its project's storage plus its path: the same relative path in two projects is two editors with their own writes and lifetimes, closing one project's documents leaves the other's, and a doubled separator names the same editor.

reason: TS rewrites `./docs\a.md`, `docs//a.md` and folder addresses into one canonical string before identity and layout use them. A native editor address is a RelativePath built from path components: `.` and `..` segments are refused, `\` is an ordinary file-name character on macOS, and a doubled separator collapses to the same key (editor_identity_is_storage_and_path_and_odd_addresses_never_alias), so there is no alternate spelling to rewrite.

acceptance: A document opens next to the active one, opening a known document again reuses it with its newer label, closing activates the most recently used remaining document, and moving one before another changes no focus history.

A project's workbench restores its order, recent use, panes and ratio after its documents are admitted, without the restore overwriting what was stored; duplicate visible documents from an old layout collapse to one pane; opening a document that is already visible focuses its pane instead of splitting; a new split pane is empty; reordering panes keeps what each shows; and a folder never becomes an editor.

reason: TS migrates its own older path-only Workbench and Pane records into Root URI records. The native app has its own identity (ADR-009) and keeps its own versioned workbench metadata keyed by the project's storage; it never reads the Electron renderer's records, so there is nothing to migrate.

acceptance: Layout and catalog changes in a burst are written once after a short delay, a lifecycle boundary writes at once, and switching to another project still writes the previous project's last change.

Dragging an editor split's edge previews the ratio as the pointer moves anywhere in the window, on either axis; Escape or leaving the window puts back the ratio it had, losing keyboard focus inside the window does not; a release commits the last position once, kept within 0.15..0.85, and a move after it changes nothing; nothing is stored while the drag previews.

reason: An editor split's handle takes no keyboard focus: there is no arrow-key adjustment on the split's own axis and no equalize command, so the ratio changes only by dragging.

acceptance: A pane's handle shows while the pointer is in its top third or its menu is open, a lone pane keeps it, and one pane menu is open at a time without a click starting a drag. Dragging the handle over another pane previews the edge it lands on (never its own pane); Escape ends the move with the layout untouched and the next press opens the menu; a release moves the pane there and keeps it focused.
One Explorer file dragged over a pane previews the nearest edge, leaving the window clears the preview, and the drop opens the file at that edge.

reason: TS marks the pane leaves that touch the bottom of the BrowserWindow so its rounded paint edge clips them. A native window clips its own corners, so panes carry no such mark.

TS activates a pane only after the pointer is released so a React re-render cannot break a DOM text selection that starts there. A native pane is activated when the press lands, as native editors do; the selection gesture is the document's own and is not interrupted.

While a pane is moved, TS shows a themed shell with a compositor snapshot of the pane following the pointer. The native drag shows a small text chip instead (the handle's tooltip text); there is no snapshot of the pane.

acceptance: In a nested three-pane split each document keeps its own editor and its edits while focus moves between panes and while panes are reordered or moved to the other axis; nothing is remounted, and switching which document shows reads no other.

reason: An empty native pane is the quiet editor canvas with only its close button: no 'Select a file to preview' prompt, no opening mark and no loading animation in the pane; a document appears in its pane once it is read (a file window shows the loading mark, without copy). A stored folder reference is dropped at restore, so its pane comes back empty rather than as an unavailable document.

acceptance: A resource-only pane's menu is Open in default app and Close (Close runs the shell's close and closes the menu); a viewer's own controls such as the PDF's Reload sit in the pane menu after that pair, not in a viewer header.
